standard.title: Specification for Pressure Ranges for Compressed Air System for Inland Vessels
standard.sector: Transport Engineering / Inland, Harbour Crafts and Fishing Vessels

sectional_committee.name: Inland, Harbour Crafts and Fishing Vessels Sectional Committee

standard.description: This standard specifies standard pressure ranges in starting-air and compressed-air systems of vessels for inland navigation. It defines standard nominal pressure values used to select equipment, machinery, and pipeline elements (such as air receivers, compressors, fittings, valves, and piping) to ensure the unification, standardization, and interchangeability of pneumatic systems in inland water transport.
standard.scope: This standard specifies standard pressure ranges in starting-air and compressed-air systems of vessels for inland navigation. It defines standard nominal pressure values used to select equipment, machinery, and pipeline elements (such as air receivers, compressors, fittings, valves, and piping) to ensure the unification, standardization, and interchangeability of pneumatic systems in inland water transport.

certification.description: Voluntary System and Performance Specification. Unlike steel constructions, builders hardware, or hazardous fluid packaging which are subject to mandatory statutory Quality Control Orders (QCOs), IS 10527 : 1983 is certified on a voluntary basis. Shipyards and marine auxiliary manufacturers who satisfy the requirements are eligible to apply for a BIS license to use the Standard Mark (ISI Mark) on air receivers, manifolds, and control valves. However, compliance with this standard is universally mandated inside all national public sector (such as Inland Waterways Authority of India - IWAI), port authority, and commercial maritime vessel procurement tenders to ensure the safety and interchangeability of pneumatic machinery.
requirements: The starting-air pressure ranges are intended strictly to guide the selection, sizing, and design of equipment, machinery, and pipeline elements (such as air receivers, compressors, fittings, and valves) for starting main and auxiliary propulsion engines or diesel generators.

The compressed-air pressure ranges cover equipment, machinery, and pipeline elements of auxiliary systems providing the operation of: blast signals, pneumatic tanks, windshield wipers, towing winch brakes, coupling locks, pneumatic control of main engines, air supply for domestic requirements, blowing Kingston valve boxes, casting off towing hooks, and releasing anchors.
Specifies nominal pressure ranges in kPa (kilopascals) for selection: 100, 125, 150, 200, 250, 300, 400, 500, 600, 700, 800, 1000, 1200, 1500, 2000, 2500.
To maintain international consistency and simplify calculation methods across mechanical, hydraulic, and structural design disciplines, the standard defines that: 100 kPa = 1 kgf/cm².

All piping manifolds, high-pressure reservoirs, steel tubes, and connecting valves used in inland vessel air systems must be designed, dimensioned, and pressure-tested to match the selected nominal values of this standard, ensuring leak-proof sealing under extreme marine humidity and rocking stresses.
